# Per-charge recharge engine in PowerUpLevelStore

## Goal

Implement the run-scoped per-charge recharge model in the single `PowerUpLevelStore`: every consumed Phase Shift / Teleport charge starts its own timer and returns when the level-derived time elapses, capped at 3, and the permanent Phase Shift hold-full reward is converted from unlimited activations to a recharging pool.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Per-charge recharge model: `consumePhaseCharge()` / `consumeTeleport()` start one independent recharge timer per consumed charge; when the level-derived time elapses the charge returns to the pool; a charge that has recharged and been spent again starts a new timer.
- Maximum charge cap of 3: the pool never exceeds 3 charges for either ability, whether collected (field pickup / hold-full reward) or recharged. Any collection or recharge that would exceed the cap is discarded.
- Level-up reduces recharge time: recharge time is level-derived via `phaseRechargeRate`/`teleportRechargeRate`; `phaseRechargeTime()`/`teleportRechargeTime()` expose seconds (`1/rate`) so higher levels recharge faster.
- Permanent Phase Shift is a recharging pool: the hold-full reward no longer grants unlimited activations; it adds one charge (up to the cap of 3) and recharges like any other charge.
- Field pickup grants one charge: collecting Phase Shift or Teleport from the field grants the level-derived grant count (`phaseCharges`/`teleportStacks` from the level catalogue), clamped so the total never exceeds 3.
- Teleport hold-full mirrors Phase Shift: +1 charge, clamped to 3, recharging normally.
- Recharge timers are run-scoped: they advance while the game runs and are cleared by `reset()` with the level store (weapon parity).

## Minimal Implementation

- `PowerUpLevelStore`: per-charge recharge-timer state, `tickRecharge(dt)`, grant/consume clamping (collect field/hold-full, recharge-complete), seconds accessors, redefinition of `_phasePermanent` as an owned flag (not unlimited), `reset()` clearing.
- Update module-header docs to describe the recharge model.

## Dependencies

- Unit tests: per-charge recharge engine and cap-3 (test-first).
- Recharge-time level axes in the power-up catalogue (axes + seconds accessors).

## Key Files

- src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts

# Tests: recharge tick, auto-defence resolver, parity

## Goal

Verify the recharge wiring through the shared tick path, the finite-pool automatic-defence resolver, and game↔gym parity before implementing the wiring (test-first; drives the wiring implementation feature).

## Acceptance Criteria

- `EffectsRegistry.tick(dt)` advances the injected level store's recharge timers so depleted Phase Shift/Teleport pools recover over time.
- `selectAutoDefence` with finite capped pools: the greater available count wins, an exact tie uses the injected-RNG 50/50, `null` when both pools are empty, and partial (mid-recharge) pools order exactly per the parent resolver rule — with no unbounded/permanent-Infinity branch.
- `updateDanger` spends a defence only when the selected pool is non-empty; an empty pool contributes zero available count.
- Scene parity: the recharge advance runs through the shared registry tick consumed by PlayScene, GymFormationScene and GymPowerUpsCombat; the duplicate-body guard / equivalence suite still passes (gym ↔ game parity).
- HUD-facing accessors (`phaseCharges()`, `teleportStacks()`, `phaseRechargeTime()`, `teleportRechargeTime()`) report recharge-aware values.

## Minimal Implementation

- Extend `src/powerups/effects.test.ts` (tick-advances-recharge, finite-pool resolver, updateDanger) and the parity suites (`src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`, `src/scenes/core/powerUpLeveling.parity.test.ts`) where the recharge path is exercised.
- No production code changes in this item (test-first) — red until the wiring implementation lands.

## Dependencies

- Per-charge recharge engine in PowerUpLevelStore (the engine must exist to tick).

## Key Files

- src/powerups/effects.test.ts
- src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts

# Wire recharge tick and finite-pool auto-defence

## Goal

Advance the store's recharge timers from the shared registry tick (the one path every scene consumes, guaranteeing parity) and convert the automatic-defence resolver from the old unlimited-permanent model to finite capped pools.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `EffectsRegistry.tick(dt)` advances the injected store's recharge timers (shared tick path → identical behaviour in the game and every gym).
- `selectAutoDefence` no longer treats any pool as unbounded: both Phase Shift and Teleport are finite pools capped at 3; ordering by greater available count and the exact-tie RNG branch are unchanged; the permanent-Phase-Shift-Infinity branch is removed.
- `updateDanger` selects a defence only when the pool is non-empty (an empty pool contributes zero available count); the shared re-arm governor and `PHASE_REARM_COOLDOWN` (0.5 s) are unchanged.
- Registry accessors (`phaseCharges()`, `teleportStacks()`, `phaseRechargeTime()`, `teleportRechargeTime()`) reflect recharge state for the HUD.
- No gameplay divergence between the game and the gyms (shared registry tick + shared resolver, duplicate-body guard green).

## Minimal Implementation

- `src/powerups/effects.ts`: tick wiring, `selectAutoDefence` signature/body (drop the permanent-Infinity semantics), HUD accessors, header docs.
- `CombatScene._updateAutoDefence` and the scene tick sites consume the registry unchanged (verify no edits needed).

## Dependencies

- Tests: recharge tick, auto-defence resolver, parity (test-first).
- Per-charge recharge engine in PowerUpLevelStore.

## Key Files

- src/powerups/effects.ts

# Tests: HUD grey-out for empty recharge pools

## Goal

Verify the greyed-out-row behaviour for zero-charge Phase Shift / Teleport pools before implementing it (test-first; drives the HUD implementation feature).

## Acceptance Criteria

- A Phase Shift or Teleport pool with zero available charges renders its HUD row greyed-out/inactive (icon + label + value) while the player owns the power-up.
- The same rows render normally when charges > 0.
- Rows for power-ups the player has never owned remain hidden, and non-charge rows render exactly as before (no regression).
- Charge-count labels reflect the recharge-aware counts (`×N`) and no longer show the unlimited marker once the permanent Phase Shift reward becomes a finite pool.

## Minimal Implementation

- Extend `src/ui/HUD.test.ts` (grey-out matrix: empty-but-owned, non-empty, not-owned; label/value expectations).
- No production code changes in this item (test-first) — red until the HUD implementation lands.

## Dependencies

- Wire recharge tick and finite-pool auto-defence (accessors must report recharge-aware counts).

## Key Files

- src/ui/HUD.test.ts

# HUD grey-out for zero-charge power-up rows

## Goal

When a power-up the player owns has zero available charges, render its HUD row (icon + label + value) greyed-out/inactive instead of hiding it; render normally when charges > 0.

## Acceptance Criteria

- When a power-up the player owns has zero available charges, its HUD row is rendered greyed-out/inactive; when charges > 0 the row renders normally.
- Row visibility: an owned Phase Shift/Teleport with an empty pool stays visible (greyed), not hidden; power-ups the player has never owned stay hidden.
- The icon, label and value share one greyed styling derived from a shared grey variant (`src/powerups/icons.ts`), so icon and text cannot diverge.
- Charged rows and all non-charge rows render unchanged.

## Minimal Implementation

- `src/ui/HUD.ts`: `_isPowerUpRowVisible` / `_powerUpStacks` (owned-but-empty → visible + greyed), `_addRow` grey styling, HUD docs.
- `src/powerups/icons.ts`: shared grey variant for the Phase Shift/Teleport icons used by the HUD.

## Dependencies

- Tests: HUD grey-out for empty recharge pools (test-first).
- Wire recharge tick and finite-pool auto-defence.

## Key Files

- src/ui/HUD.ts
- src/powerups/icons.ts

# Live thruster config carried in BotSnapshot

**Parent:** AH-0MV268RXJ007M7A9 · **Issue type:** task · **Priority:** medium

## Goal

`BotSnapshot` must carry the player's live thruster physics — forward
`thrustAcceleration`, `maxSpeed`, `frictionDeceleration` and reverse
`enabled` / `reverseAcceleration` / `reverseMaxSpeed` — sourced from the live
`Player`/`ShipConfig` via `buildBotSnapshot`, not from tunables.

As a player who tuned my ship, I want the demo bot to receive my live thruster
configuration in its decision input, so the bot flies the same physics I
configured without any code edits.

## Scope

- Add a public `Player.getThrusterConfig()` getter returning the forward and
  reverse thruster physics, mirroring the existing `getRotationConfig()`
  precedent (reads the live/effective `_config`).
- Extend `BotPlayer` in `botSnapshot.ts` (nested `thruster` object or
  flattened fields) and populate it in `buildBotSnapshot` via the structural
  `BotPlayerSource` seam — only when the source exposes it, so snapshots from
  sources without the getter keep their existing shape.
- Ensure the derived `BotWorld.player` and the pure decision layer receive the
  config unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `Player.getThrusterConfig()` returns forward thrust acceleration, max speed and friction deceleration, plus reverse enabled / acceleration / max speed, mirroring the `getRotationConfig()` precedent.
- `BotPlayer` carries the thruster physics and `buildBotSnapshot` populates it from the player source via the structural `BotPlayerSource` seam; when the source does not expose the config the field is omitted so existing fallback semantics hold.
- `BotWorld.player` and the pure decision layer receive the config unchanged from the snapshot (no re-derivation, no live game access inside steering).
- The existing demo path `PlayScene._advanceDemoBot` → `buildBotSnapshot(this)` picks the values up automatically, with no hard-coded physics in the decision layer; the `BotSnapshotScene`/`BotPlayerSource` seams are updated to match.

## Key Files

- `src/ai/botSnapshot.ts` — `BotPlayer` thruster fields, `BotPlayerSource` seam, `buildBotSnapshot` wiring.
- `src/entities/Player.ts` — new public `getThrusterConfig()` getter.
- `src/ai/framework/worldModel.ts` — confirm `BotWorld.player` carries the config unchanged.
- `src/ai/botSnapshot.test.ts` — builder tests for the new fields and the absent-config path.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — verify the demo path consumes the snapshot without other hard-coded thruster use.

## Dependencies

- Depends on AH-0MV268RXJ007M7A9's test-harness child (test-first baseline).

## Out of scope

- The steering/forward-model consumption of these values (next child).
- `assumedBulletSpeed` / `firePredictionHorizon` (enemy-bullet modelling).

## References

- Parent intake brief: AH-0MV268RXJ007M7A9
- `src/core/configTypes.ts` (`thrustAcceleration`, `maxSpeed`, `frictionDeceleration`, `asteroidsReverse*`)

# Steering and forward model consume live thruster values

**Parent:** AH-0MV268RXJ007M7A9 · **Issue type:** task · **Priority:** medium

## Goal

The steering candidate prediction (`evaluateDirection` player-speed term) and
the forward-model thrust decision (`mayThrust` friction stopping distance) must
use the snapshot's live values; the tunables `playerSpeed` /
`frictionDeceleration` become **defaults/overrides**, never authoritative.

As a designer editing `frictionDeceleration`/`maxSpeed`, I want the demo bot's
steering and stopping behaviour to track the change without code edits, so I
can validate tuning in a gym or a run.

## Scope

- `evaluateDirection`: use the snapshot's live max speed for the candidate
  speed term, falling back to tunables `playerSpeed`.
- `mayThrust`: use the snapshot's live friction deceleration for stopping
  distance, falling back to tunables `frictionDeceleration`.
- Precedence: explicit `GymBotTuning` override > live `ShipConfig` > compiled
  tunable default.
- Preserve exact default-equivalence: with no config present the decisions are
  bit-for-bit unchanged vs today.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `evaluateDirection`'s candidate-speed term uses the snapshot's live max speed when present, falling back to the `playerSpeed` tunable otherwise.
- `mayThrust` computes stopping distance with the snapshot's live friction deceleration when present, falling back to the `frictionDeceleration` tunable; explicit GymBotTuning overrides still win over live config, which wins over the compiled default (documented precedence).
- With no config in the snapshot the decisions are bit-for-bit identical to today's `playerSpeed: 175` / `frictionDeceleration: 100` constants (default-equivalence preserved).
- At least one unit test pins a pure decision consuming live values and changing the outcome versus the defaults; the fallback-path baseline test stays green.

## Key Files

- `src/ai/framework/competent/steering.ts` — `evaluateDirection`, `mayThrust`.
- `src/ai/framework/competent/tunables.ts` — `playerSpeed`/`frictionDeceleration` documented as defaults/overrides.
- `src/ai/framework/worldModel.ts` — world view carries the player config (if the term is read from the world).
- `src/ai/framework/competent/steering.test.ts` — custom-vs-default and fallback tests.
- `src/ai/framework/competent/competentBot.test.ts` — end-to-end decision coverage.

## Dependencies

- Depends on the BotSnapshot thruster-config child (AH-0MV268RXJ007M7A9).
- Depends on the test-harness child.

## Out of scope

- Reverse thrust modelling (next child).
- Enemy-bullet fire-prediction tunables.

## References

- Parent intake brief: AH-0MV268RXJ007M7A9

# Reverse braking model consumes live reverse thruster values

**Parent:** AH-0MV268RXJ007M7A9 · **Issue type:** task · **Priority:** medium

## Goal

Reverse braking must be gated and modelled with the live reverse values:
`asteroidsReverseEnabled` (already respected at snapshot level),
`asteroidsReverseThrustAcceleration` and `asteroidsReverseMaxSpeed` feed the
reverse forward-model instead of being absent.

As a player who re-tuned or disabled my reverse thruster, I want the bot's
reverse braking to use my configured acceleration and speed cap, so the demo
never contradicts the handling I experience.

## Scope

- Feed the live reverse acceleration and/or reverse speed cap into the reverse
  forward-model (brake distance under reverse acceleration and/or reverse
  speed cap).
- Keep the existing `mayReverse` tuning gates (`reverseImminentOvershootGap`,
  `reverseRetreatRange`) as tunables.
- Preserve the trouble/correction semantics from AH-0MV2WJSY70070HK2 (reverse
  is not a general positioning tool).

## Acceptance Criteria

- The reverse forward-model consumes `asteroidsReverseThrustAcceleration` and/or `asteroidsReverseMaxSpeed` from the snapshot to model reverse-assisted braking distance / reverse speed cap, instead of omitting reverse physics entirely.
- Reverse remains gated on the snapshot's live `reverseEnabled`, and the existing `mayReverse` tuning gates (`reverseImminentOvershootGap`, `reverseRetreatRange`) remain tunables.
- The reverse-reserved-for-trouble/correction semantics of AH-0MV2WJSY70070HK2 are preserved (no reverse used for routine positioning).
- Unit tests cover a custom reverse config changing the reverse decision versus defaults, and reverse-disabled behaviour emitting no reverse.

## Key Files

- `src/ai/framework/competent/steering.ts` — `mayReverse` / reverse forward-model.
- `src/ai/botSnapshot.ts` — reverse fields consumed.
- `src/ai/framework/competent/tunables.ts` — reverse gate/default docs.
- `src/ai/framework/competent/steering.test.ts` — custom reverse config + disabled tests.

## Dependencies

- Depends on the live thruster-config snapshot child.
- Depends on the test-harness child.
- Related: AH-0MV2WJSY70070HK2 (reverse overuse semantics).

## Out of scope

- A full reverse-kinematics rework beyond the live numeric consumption.

## References

- Parent intake brief: AH-0MV268RXJ007M7A9
- AH-0MV2JS18K006YU35 (reverse enable-flag plumbing)

# Tunable demotion, gym parity, docs and full-suite verification

**Parent:** AH-0MV268RXJ007M7A9 · **Issue type:** task · **Priority:** medium

## Goal

Complete the refactor: demote the physics tunables to documented defaults,
prove gym↔game parity, update the documentation, and verify the full suite.

As a maintainer, I want the tunables clearly documented as fallback defaults +
overrides, parity enforced between the demo bot and the gym, and the docs to
match the new live-thruster model.

## Scope

- `tunables.ts`: mark `playerSpeed`/`frictionDeceleration` (and any new
  reverse preview defaults) as fallback defaults + tuning overrides, never the
  ship's truth.
- Verify `GymBotTuning` / `toCompetentOverrides` overrides still win over live
  config (same `resolveCompetentTunables` seam as `PlayScene`).
- Update `docs/BOT_FRAMEWORK.md` and code comments.
- Run the full project test suite.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `tunables.ts` demotes `playerSpeed`/`frictionDeceleration` (and any new reverse preview defaults) to documented fallback defaults and tuning overrides, never authoritative, with doc comments updated.
- `GymBotTuning` overrides (`toCompetentOverrides`) demonstrably still win over live config for the fields they set, through the same `resolveCompetentTunables` seam as `PlayScene`.
- Gym↔game parity holds: `PlayScene` and the gym scenes exercising the bot share the same snapshot/steering code — no divergent copy (the repo duplicate-body guard and the gym-parity docs assertion pass).
- `docs/BOT_FRAMEWORK.md` and code comments reflect live-thruster consumption and the fallback/override precedence.
- The full project test suite passes with all changes.

## Key Files

- `src/ai/framework/competent/tunables.ts` — default/override docs.
